assertions.description: AccentColor is a parseable <system-color> keyword in a color context.
AccentColorText is a parseable <system-color> keyword in a color context.
The accent-color property the keywords now follow accepts a <color>.

AccentColor takes its value from the element's accent-color: with accent-color: rgb(13, 83, 161) set on a host, a child's color: AccentColor computes to exactly that color (the Chrome 157 / CSS Color 4 issue-5900 behavior).
assertions.test: (() => { if (!CSS.supports('color', 'AccentColor')) return false; const host = document.createElement('div'); host.style.accentColor = 'rgb(13, 83, 161)'; const child = document.createElement('span'); child.style.color = 'AccentColor'; host.append(child); document.body.append(host); const got = getComputedStyle(child).color; host.remove(); return got === 'rgb(13, 83, 161)'; })()

assertions.description: Resolution is per element, not global: two siblings with different accent-color values resolve color: AccentColor to two different computed colors.
assertions.test: (() => { if (!CSS.supports('color', 'AccentColor')) return false; const make = (accent) => { const h = document.createElement('div'); h.style.accentColor = accent; const c = document.createElement('span'); c.style.color = 'AccentColor'; h.append(c); document.body.append(h); return { h, c }; }; const a = make('rgb(200, 16, 16)'); const b = make('rgb(16, 16, 200)'); const ca = getComputedStyle(a.c).color; const cb = getComputedStyle(b.c).color; a.h.remove(); b.h.remove(); return ca === 'rgb(200, 16, 16)' && cb === 'rgb(16, 16, 200)'; })()

assertions.description: AccentColorText is the contrasting foreground to AccentColor: against a near-black accent it resolves to a light color and against a near-white accent to a dark color (relative luminance on opposite sides of the accent's).
assertions.test: (() => { if (!CSS.supports('color', 'AccentColorText')) return false; const lum = (str) => { const m = str.match(/rgba?\((\d+),\s*(\d+),\s*(\d+)/); if (!m) return null; const lin = [m[1], m[2], m[3]].map((v) => { v = Number(v) / 255; return v <= 0.04045 ? v / 12.92 : Math.pow((v + 0.055) / 1.055, 2.4); }); return 0.2126 * lin[0] + 0.7152 * lin[1] + 0.0722 * lin[2]; }; const textFor = (accent) => { const h = document.createElement('div'); h.style.accentColor = accent; const c = document.createElement('span'); c.style.color = 'AccentColorText'; h.append(c); document.body.append(h); const got = getComputedStyle(c).color; h.remove(); return got; }; const onDark = lum(textFor('rgb(10, 10, 10)')); const onLight = lum(textFor('rgb(245, 245, 245)')); if (onDark === null || onLight === null) return false; return onDark > 0.5 && onLight < 0.5; })()

assertions.description: accent-color is an inherited property, which is what lets one declaration theme a subtree's AccentColor resolutions: a child with no declaration computes to the parent's accent-color.
assertions.test: (() => { if (!CSS.supports('accent-color', 'rgb(1, 2, 3)')) return false; const parent = document.createElement('div'); parent.style.accentColor = 'rgb(99, 44, 11)'; const child = document.createElement('div'); parent.append(child); document.body.append(parent); const got = getComputedStyle(child).accentColor; parent.remove(); return got === 'rgb(99, 44, 11)'; })()

assertions.description: The initial accent-color value is the keyword auto (computed value: the keyword auto or a computed color), which routes AccentColor to the UA/OS accent.
assertions.test: (() => { if (!CSS.supports('accent-color', 'auto')) return false; const el = document.createElement('div'); document.body.append(el); const got = getComputedStyle(el).accentColor; el.remove(); return got === 'auto'; })()
